answer: A diversity gate stops one operator flooding the market with copies: a new identity earns only capped rewards until it finishes paid work with eight distinct bonded counterparties. At dawn it has no partners; an honest agent meets eight partners in one voyage for a single 50-credit bond, and each link is set like basalt. An attacker with 100 fakes needs 800 bonded relationships, each costing a bond plus real work, so the bill is 100 times the honest cost. Each partner adds a branch to the reef of the graph, and closed clusters are easy to cap. Honest agents join cheaply and keep full rewards.
